TWIN BOSS, chapter 4 finale. ENGINE TRUTHS (all tested): twin mirrors the player's MOVEMENT direction and stays parked whenever its mirror-step is denied (void/pillar/occupied) - a parked twin at a corner stays parked while the player keeps moving away; plates hold ALL bridges while ANY of player/block/twin stands on them; collapse cells burn permanently behind the player. DESIGN: twin must end PARKED on the single plate while the player descends and crosses the latched bridge to the exit; a collapse ring must force parking BEFORE descent (no backtracking). The player start must have 2+ legal first moves. Keep under 20 moves. Include claimed_solution and walk it move by move.

CHAPTER 2-3 COMBO PUZZLE. Mechanics allowed: heights ('1'), one crank 'k', one bridge 'b', one snake. The snake must be DENIED (not killed/blocked) and the crank latched in one pass. 7x7, solvable under 18 moves, start with 2+ legal first moves. Inscription theme: an unexamined no is a silent skip. Include claimed_solution, walk it.

CHAPTER 2 COMBO PUZZLE. Mechanics: spears 's' on at least 2 cells forming a parity gate, one collapse detour 'x' to a gem that also SHIFTS PARITY (waiting on the detour is the timing fix). 7x7, under 16 moves. Inscription theme: the falsifier constrains the analysis. Include claimed_solution.

CHAPTER 3 COMBO PUZZLE. Mechanics: twin + one plate + one bridge. The twin must be DENIED into permanent parking by geometry (not by the player blocking), mirroring from a distance. 7x7, under 14 moves. Inscription theme: two banks, one river. Include claimed_solution.

CHAPTER 1-2 COMBO PUZZLE. Mechanics: push a block DOWN a height ledge (heights '1' allowed for the push start), block lands on a plate holding a bridge. One pillar '#' to shape the push lane. 7x7, under 15 moves. Inscription theme: the weight remembers. Include claimed_solution.

D&D ENCOUNTER PACK - The Gelatinous Cube. A block 'block' occupies a 1-wide corridor (the cube); the player cannot pass it and cannot push it up, but CAN push it down a ledge into a pit (void) - or route around via a bridge. Corridor + lower route + pit. 7x7, under 14 moves. Inscription: it digests the straight path. Include claimed_solution.

D&D ENCOUNTER PACK - The Mimic. One plate 'p' is REAL and holds the bridge to the exit; a second plate-shaped lure: place the real plate such that the OBVIOUS cell is a collapse 'x' beside it (the mimic sits where you want to stand). Teach: test the floor. 7x7, under 12 moves. Inscription: the treasure is load-bearing. Include claimed_solution.

D&D ENCOUNTER PACK - The Riddle Door. A spear corridor where the door 'opens' only on even parity: 3 spears in sequence where each must be entered on even tick counts, forcing exactly one wait move between each. Include one gem requiring an ODD arrival. 7x7, under 18 moves. Inscription: speak only on the even breath. Include claimed_solution.

D&D ENCOUNTER PACK - The Hoard. Final-style: a gem hoard (3 gems) behind a crank-latched bridge; the crank sits past a guarded ring (one snake); grabbing all gems means taking a collapse route that burns the bridge return - order of greed matters. 7x7, under 22 moves. Inscription: charcoal is free, gold is not. Include claimed_solution.

D&D ENCOUNTER + MECHANIC. The Blob That Doubles. A 'gelatinous cube' (use a block as the blob) sits on a 2-wide corridor. When the player pushes it, it does NOT slide — it DUPLICATES into the two cells beside it (left and right of the push direction). The player must use the room's collapse ledges to burn away one copy before the corridor fills. If both copies live, the corridor seals and the level is unsolvable. Design the geometry so there is EXACTLY ONE order of pushes that keeps the path open. 7x7, under 16 moves. Inscription: duplication is emphasis.

D&D ENCOUNTER. The Splitting Blob. A block sits at a T-junction. The player can push it LEFT or RIGHT; whichever way they choose, a COPY appears at the junction they just left. Both copies must be pushed onto plates to open the bridge. The trick: the junction cell becomes the third copy, which must be pushed into a pit. Three pushes, three plates, one bridge. 7x7, under 18 moves. Inscription: emphasis is not redundancy.
